title: Phylogenetics and taxonomy of the African flatnose catfishes (Auchenoglanididae) revisited: a total evidence approach
content:
Abstract
The morphologically diverse African catfish family Auchenoglanididae has recently been restricted to include only the genera Auchenoglanis, Parauchenoglanis, and Notoglanidium. We conducted a phylogenetic analysis integrating genomic data from ultraconserved elements (UCEs) and a morphological dataset of 61 anatomical characters to further investigate generic composition and intrarelationships of this poorly known assemblage. Our results indicate that species assigned to Notoglanidium do not form a monophyletic group, necessitating the resurrection of two previously synonymized genera. We find that N. maculatum, N. thomasi, and N. walkeri form a clade sister to all other members of the Auchenoglanididae and restrict Notoglanidium to these three species. We additionally recognize Anaspidoglanis to include An. boutchangai and An. macrostoma, and Platyglanis to include Pl. depierrei and Pl. pembetadi, and redefine the species rich genus Parauchenoglanis to include the cryptophthalmic lower Congo River endemic Pa. pallidum.
